xray.panel.intro: Dashed boxes are React components. Each label counts how many times that component has rendered, and flashes when it does. Click a label to read why it’s built that way.
xray.hud.title: Performance
xray.hud.dev: Bundle sizes appear in the production build.
xray.note.header: One page, so no router: plain #anchors and CSS scroll-margin-top handle navigation. Not adding a dependency is a decision too.
xray.note.themeToggle: The theme is a class on the html element, not React state at the top of the tree, so switching re-renders exactly one component: this button. Colors are CSS variables, and a tiny inline script in index.html applies the saved theme before first paint, so it never flashes.
xray.note.langToggle: Switching language re-renders everything that reads from react-intl, so watch the counters jump. The layout flips through dir="rtl" and logical utilities like ps-4 instead of pl-4, so components barely need RTL-specific code. Only directional icons get mirrored.
xray.note.hero: The headline doesn’t fade in, on purpose. Text that starts at opacity: 0 can delay Largest Contentful Paint, so only content below the fold animates. Fonts are self-hosted, and the Arabic font downloads only when Arabic text appears, thanks to unicode-range.
xray.note.project: The board preview is HTML and CSS, not a screenshot, so it stays sharp at any size, follows the theme and flips in Arabic. HireFlow itself uses row-level security in Postgres, so permissions are enforced by the database, not just hidden in the UI.
xray.note.experience: Content lives in typed files in src/data, with English and Arabic side by side. A missing translation is a TypeScript error, not a bug a visitor finds. Dates are formatted with Intl.DateTimeFormat, so month names follow the language.
xray.note.skillsLab: Each keystroke re-renders this section. With React.memo on, a card re-renders only when its own props change. That works because its props are a stable object from static data and a string, with no inline objects or functions. React Compiler would memoize this automatically; it’s off here so you can see the difference.
xray.note.skillCard: This count goes up only when this card actually renders.
xray.note.contact: No form and no backend: a mailto link and a static PDF. The part of the page that matters most has the fewest moving parts.
xray.note.perfHud: This panel is loaded with React.lazy only when X-ray turns on, so visitors who never press X never download it. Web Vitals are recorded from page load into a small store read with useSyncExternalStore. Bundle sizes are real: a small Vite plugin gzips the build output and writes build-stats.json.
xray.note.dock: How the counters work: each Inspect wrapper compares its children with the last render. New children means the component that owns it re-rendered. A render caused only by X-ray itself keeps the same children, so it isn’t counted. The number is written to the DOM in a layout effect, so counting never causes extra renders. The X shortcut checks event.code, so it works on an Arabic keyboard too.
